title: sh says /sh/
parentNote: Yesterday two letters shared a sound your child already had. Today two letters make a sound that is genuinely new: sh is not /s/ and it is not /h/, it is /shhh/ — the noise you make asking for quiet — and neither of the letters can be heard in it. That is what makes it different from something like sk in "skip", where you really do hear both sounds one after the other; here you hear one sound and one sound only. The error, almost every time, is reading the letters separately, so "ship" becomes "s-hip"; cover the h with a finger and ask what is left, then uncover it and say the whole thing as one long hiss. For the mouth: /s/ is a thin sharp hiss with the tongue forward, /shhh/ is wide and soft with the lips pushed out — say sip and ship back to back and let them watch your lips move.

activities.mouthCue: Teeth nearly shut, lips pushed forward, tongue pulled back a little. The air comes out wide and soft — shhhhh.
